content: 1. The involvement of national non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in dementia-related policy development is assessed to determine whether they are formally engaged in creating or implementing policies, laws, or regulations. This includes participation in the development of national dementia plans or consultation for dementia legislation. 2. The creation and implementation of services and support for dementia carers aim to address their needs and prevent deterioration in their physical and mental health, as well as their social well-being. These services include training programs, respite care, and other resources tailored to carers' needs. 3. Functional carer support programs are defined as those with dedicated financial and human resources, an implementation plan, and documented evidence of progress or impact. 4. Carer training and education programs focus on improving carers' knowledge and skills in dementia management, including care techniques, nonverbal communication, and fostering patient-carer relationships throughout the disease's progression. 5. Psychosocial support for carers includes support groups, online resources, peer-to-peer networks, counseling, and helplines, which are available throughout the disease course and beyond the death of the person with dementia. 6. Respite services provide carers with time away from their caregiving role, allowing them to engage in other activities while ensuring the care recipient receives quality care. 7. Legal and financial support for carers includes information on legal rights, employment protection, carers' benefits, paid or unpaid leave, and subsidies such as tax allowances or discounted transportation fares. 8. Dementia awareness and risk-reduction campaigns are tailored to cultural contexts and community needs. These campaigns aim to improve understanding of dementia, reduce stigma, educate about human rights, and promote healthy lifestyles to reduce risk factors. 9. Dementia-friendly initiatives focus on creating inclusive physical and social environments that enable people with dementia to participate in the community, maximize autonomy, and improve quality of life for both individuals with dementia and their carers. 10. Accessibility improvements in dementia-friendly initiatives include modifications to public spaces, transportation, home environments, and the provision of assistive technologies to support individuals with dementia and their carers. 11. Dementia education and training for non-health professionals aim to raise awareness and understanding of dementia within the wider community, considering cultural contexts and specific audience needs.
